candidateEvents.mechanismNote: No event bus, message queue, or outbox table exists anywhere in the codebase today (confirmed by grep across server/src for Queue|EventEmitter|outbox|bullmq scoped to imaging paths — the only hits are the 'unlinked queue' UI concept, a DB filter, not a real queue). errorContract.400: Zod schema validation failure; malformed multipart (missing boundary); file-signature/MIME mismatch; ingestKey does not match recomputed file hash; patient/appointment/treatmentCase mismatch against a bound ImagingRequest
errorContract.401: bridge token missing/invalid/revoked — always a generic message, never distinguishes 'agent not found' from 'token wrong' (no enumeration oracle, per IMG-01 evidence)
errorContract.403: clinic access denied (resolveEffectiveClinicId / validateAndGetClinicIdScope failure) or role not in the route's required role set
errorContract.404: entity not found within the resolved clinic scope (device, request, study, image, pairing, bridge agent, or file-in-storage) — used deliberately in place of 403 for cross-tenant lookups to avoid confirming existence to an unauthorized caller
errorContract.409: state-machine conflict (ImagingRequest not open for new studies; device/bridge-agent has dependents preventing delete; pairing already redeemed/expired/locked) — several of these are re-checked inside a row-locked $transaction, not just at the initial read
errorContract.413: Multer file-size limit exceeded (bridge upload path)
errorContract.415: preview requested for a MIME type not on the inline-preview allowlist (download is always allowed regardless of type)
errorContract.429: rate limit exceeded — IP-scoped and token-scoped heartbeat/upload limiters, plus an in-process per-token concurrency slot cap (bridge upload path only)
errorContract.500: unexpected failure; response body is a generic {error} with no stack trace; server-side console.error carries the detail

idempotencyRules.rule: Idempotent per (clinicId, ingestKey) where ingestKey = sha256(file bytes), enforced first as a pre-check read (returns duplicate:true fast path) and authoritatively by a @@unique([clinicId, ingestKey]) Postgres constraint (P2002 caught, race loser's just-written storage file is deleted, the pre-existing winner's studyId is returned).

Not idempotent by design. ingestKey is not collected on this path (manual upload); NULL values in a Postgres unique index never collide with each other, so uploading the same file twice via this route creates two independent ImagingStudy/ImagingImage rows.

idempotencyRules.rule: Naturally idempotent (repeat calls with the same target state are no-op-equivalent single-field writes); not enforced by a dedicated idempotency key, just by the field being a simple enum/boolean.

backwardCompatibilityRequirements: No existing route path, method, request shape, or response shape may change as a side effect of drafting or later adopting this contract — this task changes documentation only.

Expand-migrate-contract only: any future implementation introduces a named contract alongside existing direct-call paths (expand), migrates callers one at a time (migrate), and removes the old path only once every caller has moved (contract) — never a simultaneous cutover, per F2-PREP-005 Section 14.

Allowed inbound callers to Imaging's owned models, per F2-PREP-005 Section 10, must remain functionally unchanged: Patients (read-only enrichment via ListPatientImaging), Privacy (KVKK lifecycle fields on ImagingImage/ImagingStudy — an accepted, documented exception, not a violation to be closed by this contract).

Forbidden direct access rule must be preserved: no domain outside Imaging (and the documented Privacy exception) may write directly to Imaging's owned Prisma models; imagingBridgePublic.ts must keep deriving clinicId only from the server-matched agent record, never client input.
All of Imaging's own $transaction sites remain domain-internal (a property already true today) and must not regress.
legalHoldReason redaction (roleCanSeeLegalHoldReason / redactStudyLegalHoldReason) must be preserved on every response surface, independent of any future contract layer.

Storage-key derivation (clinicId-prefixed) and the never-a-public-URL streaming access pattern must be preserved; fileStorage.ts remains shared infrastructure, not something this contract takes ownership of.

This contract's own PZ-IMG-02 (inventory race, out of Imaging's boundary) and PZ-IMG-03 (backup/restore RBAC, unverified) are explicitly not resolved or claimed resolved by this task, per F2-PREP-005 Section 10/14.

assumptions: The suggested command/query taxonomy in the task prompt is illustrative, not authoritative — this document maps each suggested name to the closest evidence-grounded reality and explicitly flags names with no current backing (RequestImagingProcessing, UpdateProcessingStatus as a distinct concept, GetImagingProcessingResult, ExportImagingEvidence as an Imaging-owned command, RequestSecureImagingAccess as a token-issuing command) rather than inventing unevidenced behavior.
Route line numbers cited throughout are accurate as of the frozen baseline commit 4cb334d213b4dbbac4193f1a8c1878deddb55714 and may drift on main; F2-PREP-006-E should re-verify before final adoption.

Test-level assignments (unit-mock vs db-integration vs live-storage) assume the disposable-Postgres runtime pattern already established by F1-003-P2A is reusable as-is for Imaging; this was not independently re-verified against that task's exact provisioning script.
evidenceGaps: No auditImaging() (or any audit) call was found in the IngestImagingStudy route handler (server/src/routes/imagingBridgePublic.ts:199-360+), unlike CreateImagingStudy's explicit auditImaging('imaging_study_uploaded') call — this asymmetry is not explained by any doc read for this task and should be confirmed as intentional (bridge ingest volume may be considered non-audit-worthy) or flagged as a real gap by F2-PREP-006-E.

GetImagingStudy, ListPatientImaging, ListImagingRequests, and ListUnlinkedImagingStudies show no evidence of pagination; for clinics with large imaging volumes this may already be a real (pre-existing, not contract-introduced) scalability gap, out of scope to fix here but worth flagging.

Idempotency behavior for SetImagingLegalHold/ArchiveImagingStudy/UnarchiveImagingStudy is inferred from the field/schema shape, not from a line-by-line read of every route body — flagged as a soft gap, not a hard unresolved question.

The exact deleteFile() orphan-detection story when a storage-compensation delete itself fails (imaging.ts:684, .catch(() => {})) was not traced end-to-end against orphanFileInspection.ts to confirm the forward case (orphaned file with no DB row) is eventually detected the same way the inverse case (DB row with a missing file) is via storageVerifiedMissingAt.
unresolvedQuestions: Should ImagingBridgePairingDevice gain its own clinicId/organizationId column (F2-PREP-004's recommended additive fix) before or independently of this contract's eventual adoption? This task takes no position — it is a schema change, explicitly out of scope here.
Is the audit-call asymmetry between CreateImagingStudy and IngestImagingStudy intentional? See evidenceGaps.

Should ExportImagingEvidence exist as an Imaging-owned command at all, or should the contract formally document imaging-data export as permanently Privacy-owned (current reality) with Imaging exposing only the read queries Privacy already calls? This task leans toward the latter but defers the final call to F2-PREP-006-E.

What is the correct forward-compatible mechanism for ImagingStudyReceived (in-process call vs. outbox table vs. something else) given no event infrastructure exists today? Explicitly deferred, not decided, by this task.
